A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same confidence-estimation framework. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Q&A and summarization evaluations, feature-importance and cross-LLM transfer results, plus appendix experiments on perturbation validity and training-set size.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds GPT-4 evaluations, calibration measurements, decoding-budget tests, equal-query comparisons and GPT-4-judged summarization results.

M1.justification: The six elicitation strategies, semantic/lexical/SRC features and logistic-regression confidence estimator remain unchanged. Section 3 adds explanatory examples; the additional model evaluations and scoring variants do not establish a revision of the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CoQA, SQuAD, TriviaQA and NQ question answering, plus CNN/DailyMail and XSUM summarization. GPT-4 adds an evaluated model, and GPT-4 judging changes evaluation procedures; neither introduces new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The central comparisons add semantic entropy (SE) and average verbalized confidence (AVC) alongside all five existing comparators (v2 Tables 2–3; v3 Tables 3–5). This substantially broadens comparison methods, particularly by introducing a directly verbalized-confidence alternative.

E3.justification: v3 adds GPT-4 model evaluations, ECE as a third metric, three-decoding variants, equal-query-budget controls and GPT-4 judging of summaries. These are additional evaluation protocols; the original validation splits, 1,000-example training size and main five-generation setting are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine decoding-budget sensitivity, whether advantages survive equal query budgets, and robustness to alternative summary judging (v3 Tables 6 and 11–15). Existing training-size, feature-importance and transfer analyses are expanded to GPT-4, with NQ also added to the training-size study. The perturbation-validity analysis is retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Section 4 changes the reported averaging from three runs to five and introduces standard deviations rounded to three decimals for the proposed method in Tables 3–4. This is a limited expansion of repetition and dispersion reporting; deviations are not supplied for every entry or for baselines.

E6.justification: Original main-table AUROC/AUARC means are retained, while substantial results are added for GPT-4, new baselines, ECE, budget controls, alternative judging and expanded analyses. On TriviaQA/Llama, Ours remains 0.88, but AVC scores 0.79 versus v2's best baseline of 0.77, narrowing the margin from 11 to 9 percentage points (v2 Table 2; v3 Table 3).

T1.justification: The formal confidence-estimation problem in Equation 1 and its assumptions remain unchanged. v3 adds no theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation; its feature examples and ECE description are explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the efficacy claim to GPT-4, and the discussion changes the scope from five open-source LLMs to six LLMs. The central contributions—black-box confidence estimation, interpretable features and cross-LLM transfer—retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Section 5 qualifies the existing concern about ROUGE-based correctness by presenting GPT-4 judging as corroboration of the summarization conclusions. The feature-based mechanism explanations, supervision requirement and English-language limitation otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A documents which Q&A prompts GPT-4 uses and supplies its summary-similarity judging prompt. Section 4 specifies averaging five estimates for AVC. Existing hardware disclosures and baseline-code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the GPT-4 technical report and two selective-classification references, with a brief suggestion to adapt selective classification in future work. The related-work narrative remains largely unchanged; the sources for newly evaluated SE and AVC were already cited in v2.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 is renamed from 'Prompt Perturbations' to 'Elicitation of Variable LLM Behavior,' and Section 3.2 gains concrete feature examples. Local grammar corrections and expanded experimental descriptions accompany the revision, while the main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The result displays gain baseline columns, GPT-4 rows and a third transfer-target column, alongside new calibration, decoding-budget and appendix comparison tables. v2 appendix Tables 7–8 move into the main text as v3 Tables 2 and 7, with the latter expanded. Figure 1 remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 claimed calibrated confidence while reporting only discrimination and rejection metrics. v3 adds direct ECE evidence, equal-query controls and alternative-judge checks, substantially strengthening the central empirical justification. GPT-4 and additional baselines further strengthen comparison coverage. These gains outweigh limited reporting flaws, including incomplete standard-deviation coverage and the stale 11-point TriviaQA/Llama claim, now 9 points in Table 3.
